contents.name: 1B. The syntax of First Order Logic (FOL)
contents.support: Set signatures and finite constructor syntax.

contents.name: Definition 1B.1
contents.support: Signature is a set; finite positive arities.

contents.name: Definition 1B.2
contents.support: Alphabet, finite words and concatenation.

contents.name: Definition 1B.3 (Terms and formulas)
contents.support: Grammar with equality, functions, relations, connectives and quantifiers.

contents.name: Proposition 1B.4 (Parsing for terms)
contents.support: Unique immediate term decomposition.

contents.name: Proposition 1B.5 (Parsing for formulas)
contents.support: Unique formula decomposition licenses structural induction.

contents.name: Definition 1B.6 (Free and bound variables)
contents.support: FV recursion, occurrences, sentences and universal closure.

contents.name: 1B.7. Abbreviations and misspellings
contents.support: Display notation must expand into the chosen grammar.

contents.name: Definition 1B.8 (Substitution)
contents.support: Free-for qualification; simultaneous substitution differs from sequential.

contents.name: Definition 1B.9 (Extended expressions)
contents.support: A displayed variable list accompanies an expression; full lists contain all FV.

contents.name: 1B.10. First order logic without identity
contents.support: Equality-free fragment used only in the strong-surjection clause.

contents.name: 1C. Semantics of FOL
contents.support: Set carriers, assignments and recursive semantics.

contents.name: Definition 1C.1 (Structures)
contents.support: Nonempty carrier and interpreted set signature.

contents.name: Definition 1C.2 (Substructures)
contents.support: Restrictions and closure of interpreted functions.

contents.name: Definition 1C.3 (Sublanguages)
contents.support: Signature inclusion preserves symbol kind and arity.

contents.name: Definition 1C.4 (Expansions and reducts)
contents.support: Same carrier with extra or fewer symbol interpretations.

contents.name: Definition 1C.5 (Assignments)
contents.support: Variable maps and single-variable updates.

contents.name: Definition 1C.6 (Truth values)
contents.support: Truth values 0 and 1, equivalently subsets of assignment space.

contents.name: Definition 1C.7 (Denotations and satisfaction)
contents.support: Recursive denotation followed by formula truth.

contents.name: Theorem 1C.8 (The Tarski truth conditions)
contents.support: Atomic and Boolean clauses; quantified witnesses stay in carrier.

contents.name: Theorem 1C.9 (Compositionality)
contents.support: Both reduct invariance and agreement on FV.

contents.name: Definition 1C.10 (Validity and semantic consequence)
contents.support: Validity in every structure/assignment and semantic implication.

contents.name: Definition 1C.11 (Homomorphisms and isomorphisms)
contents.support: Includes strong maps, embeddings, automorphisms and rigidity as inline terminology.

contents.name: Proposition 1C.12
contents.support: All clauses: term preservation, equality-free strong-surjection truth, isomorphism invariance.

contents.name: Problem x1.1
contents.support: Term prefix lemma supplies parsing proof.

contents.name: Problem x1.2
contents.support: Parenthesis and prefix argument for formulas.

contents.name: Problem x1.3.1
contents.support: Term and formula substitution theorem; term case separately scaffolded.

contents.name: Problem x1.3.2
contents.support: Adapt arithmetic instance to two-element constant/equality structure.

contents.name: Problem x1.3.3
contents.support: Logical equivalence is preserved by free substitution.

contents.name: Problem x1.4
contents.support: Proof obligation for Proposition 1C.12.

contents.name: Problem app3 (Functional closure)
contents.support: Finite-stage constructor closure and leastness.

contents.name: Problem app4 (Structural recursion)
contents.support: Injective constructors with disjoint ranges yield unique recursion.

contents.name: Problem app5
contents.support: Apply constructor theorem to formula syntax and FV.

contents.name: Chapter 1. LOST

contents.support: Primitive versus derived connectives; bounded quantifier notation.

contents.support: Free/bound occurrences, subformulas and fresh renaming with first unused variable.

contents.support: Exact capture mechanism; scaffold uses the existential conjunct as minimal witness.

contents.name: Equality Principle (unnumbered)
contents.support: Equivalent formulas after replacement by equal values.

contents.name: Class terms and term substitution (unnumbered)
contents.support: Classes are syntactic abbreviations, eliminated using fresh variables.

contents.name: Relativisation of a Formula to a Term
contents.support: Guard every quantifier; leave atomic formulas unchanged.

contents.name: Empty-class relativisation examples (unnumbered)
contents.support: Existential truth fails for empty class while universal equality remains true.

contents.name: Chapter 11. Reflection: opening model notation
contents.support: Formula-by-formula class notation and parameters in domain.

contents.name: Theorem 43
contents.support: Membership-isomorphic sets agree on sentences.

contents.name: Lemma Psi in proof of Theorem 43
contents.support: Strengthen induction to formulas with parameters, then specialize to sentences.

contents.name: Soundness discussion at end of LOST
contents.support: A formal calculus would turn logical-inference preservation under relativization into soundness.
contents.reason: Formal derivations and their soundness are the explicit SET-2 proof spine; the present semantics does not use them.
